# Grand Task Office — Project Plan

## 1. Project summary

**Grand Task Office** is a short, shared-screen office adventure for 4–6 players. Players explore a simplified comic-style office map, receive funny missions generated by a local AI model, vote on choices, collect useful objects, and attempt to finish five missions without reaching five boss-alert stars.

This is an individual project built by one developer in collaboration with AI tools. The other participants are creating their own separate games. The development goal is to use AI throughout planning, design, implementation, content generation, testing, and presentation preparation.

**Tagline:** Complete the mission. Avoid the boss. Escape the office.

The complete application runs locally:

```text
Expo + React Native app → Flask backend → Ollama → gemma3:4b
```

No internet connection, external API key, database, account system, or multiplayer server is required.

## 2. Core game loop

1. Enter the first names of 4–6 players.
2. Select one of six areas on the office map.
3. Receive a short AI-generated mission with exactly three choices.
4. Discuss the situation and vote verbally.
5. Select the winning choice and reveal its consequence.
6. Update money, reputation, boss-alert stars, and inventory.
7. Animate any awarded object into the inventory bar.
8. Continue until five missions are completed or the alert level reaches five stars.

A complete game should last approximately 5–10 minutes.

### Endings

- Five alert stars: **Fired by the Boss**
- High reputation: **Office Legend**
- High money: **Promoted**
- Balanced surviving score: **Successful Escape**
- Complete the hidden final mission: **Master of the Office**

## 3. Office map

The supplied floor plan, building exterior, visual-identity reference, and meeting-room photograph will be used as visual references for a newly generated map.

The full third floor will be simplified into six clickable zones:

- Entrance and lifts
- Open workspace
- Meeting-room corridor
- Coffee and kitchen area
- Print and utility area
- Manager/drop-in office

The map will preserve the recognizable central corridor, perimeter offices, meeting rooms, coffee points, lifts, and emergency exits while removing unnecessary architectural detail.

### Visual direction

- Original comic-style, top-down illustration
- Terracotta orange, blue glass, charcoal, cream, and teal palette
- Black furniture, concrete columns, pendant lights, wood flooring, and large windows
- Bold mission cards, dramatic shadows, status bars, and five alert stars
- No real company names, tenant logos, room numbers, or confidential information
- No copied GTA logos, fonts, characters, maps, or artwork

The map is exported as one landscape PNG. React Native will position responsive, transparent `Pressable` hotspots over the six zones. No tileset, 3D environment, character animation, or physics system is required.

## 4. Useful objects and animation

The game supports six collectible objects:

- `cinnamon_bun`
- `coffee`
- `laptop`
- `keycard`
- `stapler`
- `secret_document`

The six objects are supplied as an original transparent 3 × 2 PNG sprite sheet. The sheet will be cropped into six individual PNG files during implementation so the icons work consistently on web, iOS, and Android. When a choice awards an object, its icon appears at the selected office zone, moves toward the inventory bar using React Native's built-in `Animated` API, and remains visible in the inventory.

Collected objects unlock special choices in later missions. Examples include using coffee to distract a colleague, a laptop to access a system remotely, or a keycard to enter a restricted area.

Rules for item choices:

- At most one of the three mission choices may require an item.
- The required item must already exist in the inventory.
- An item-powered choice is labelled **ITEM OPTION**.
- Selecting it consumes the required item.
- A choice may consume an item or award an item, but not both.
- Unknown item identifiers are ignored safely.
- Reduced-motion mode adds objects immediately without animation.

## 5. Three additional fun features

### Player names

Players enter 4–6 first names on the start screen. The names are included in the AI prompt so missions can mention the group, for example: “Bobby accidentally locked the presentation laptop in the manager’s office.” Names remain local and are not persisted.

### Funny achievements

At the end, deterministic frontend rules award humorous titles based on the game state and collected items. Initial achievements include:

- **Coffee Criminal** — collect or use the coffee
- **Stapler King** — finish with the stapler
- **Office Legend** — finish with high reputation
- **Definitely Getting Fired** — reach five alert stars
- **Master Thief** — collect at least three different objects

### Secret room

Collecting both the keycard and secret document unlocks a hidden hotspot on the map. Selecting it starts a special final mission. Completing that mission produces the **Master of the Office** ending. The secret room does not count as one of the normal six zones and remains invisible until unlocked.

## 6. Expo and React Native frontend

Create the application with Expo's default TypeScript template. The default template already includes Expo Router and is intended for multi-screen Android, iOS, and web applications.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest frontend --template default
```

Use a deliberately small Expo stack:

- **Expo Router:** file-based navigation between setup, map, mission, secret-room, and ending screens
- **TypeScript:** shared types for game state, missions, choices, items, and API responses
- **React Native core:** `View`, `Text`, `TextInput`, `Pressable`, `Image`, `ImageBackground`, `ActivityIndicator`, `StyleSheet`, and `Animated`
- **Expo StatusBar:** simple status-bar styling supplied by the Expo template
- **React hooks:** `useReducer`, `useState`, `useContext`, and `useEffect`

Route structure:

```text
src/app/_layout.tsx      Shared GameProvider and Stack
src/app/index.tsx        Player setup and title screen
src/app/map.tsx          Interactive office map
src/app/mission.tsx      Mission choices and outcome
src/app/secret-room.tsx  Hidden final mission
src/app/ending.tsx       Ending and achievements
```

Store shared game state in a small React Context and reducer outside the route files. The layout wraps every route with the provider so state survives navigation.

The primary demonstration target is Expo Web on the laptop:

```bash
npx expo start --web
```

Do not add a third-party UI framework, Redux, or an animation package. The custom game artwork and React Native core components are sufficient, keep the interface consistent, and make the React Native learning visible. `@expo/ui` can be explored after the demo but is not required for this game.

## 7. Python and Ollama backend

Use a minimal Flask service with one gameplay endpoint:

```text
POST /api/mission
```

The endpoint sends the current game context to Ollama at:

```text
http://localhost:11434/api/chat
```

Use the installed `gemma3:4b` model and request a structured JSON response. The backend validates the response, requires exactly three choices, clamps numeric effects, and rejects unsupported item values.

### Request

```json
{
  "location": "Coffee and kitchen area",
  "round": 2,
  "money": 10,
  "reputation": 4,
  "alertLevel": 1,
  "visitedLocations": ["Entrance and lifts"],
  "inventory": ["keycard"],
  "players": ["Alex", "Sam", "Kim", "Robin"]
}
```

### Response

```json
{
  "title": "The Last Cinnamon Bun",
  "situation": "Sam discovers the boss reserved the final bun, but the team is starving.",
  "choices": [
    {
      "text": "Use the keycard to reach the private snack cupboard",
      "outcome": "The cupboard opens, revealing the boss's emergency snack supply.",
      "moneyChange": 1,
      "reputationChange": 2,
      "alertChange": 0,
      "requiredItem": "keycard",
      "rewardItem": null
    }
  ]
}
```

Prepared fallback missions must keep the game playable when Ollama is stopped, slow, missing the model, or returns invalid JSON. Set `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:5000` for the laptop web demo. Configure Flask CORS only for the local Expo development origin. If the app is later tested on a physical phone, change the URL to the Mac's local network address; this is optional and not required for the presentation.

## 8. Implementation steps

Complete these milestones in order. A milestone can begin as soon as its dependencies are ready; the steps are not tied to particular days.

### AI-assisted workflow

- **Codex:** brainstorming, requirements, project planning, reviewing decisions, and maintaining documentation
- **Image generation:** transforming the supplied office references into an original comic-style game map
- **GitHub Copilot:** implementing and explaining the Expo, React Native, TypeScript, and Flask code milestone by milestone
- **Ollama with `gemma3:4b`:** generating missions dynamically while the finished game is running
- **Developer:** directing the tools, making product decisions, reviewing generated work, running the application, and accepting each result

### Step 1 — Foundation ✅ Complete

- Scaffold the Expo default TypeScript application and Flask backend.
- Keep Expo Router from the default template and replace its example routes with the game's five screens.
- Add scripts for starting both services locally.
- Confirm Flask can reach the running Ollama service and `gemma3:4b` model.

Completion record: Copilot created `frontend/` with Expo SDK 57, React Native, TypeScript, and Expo Router; `backend/` with Flask, Ollama communication, validation, three fallback missions, and a Python virtual environment; three launcher scripts; and complete setup and foundation documentation. The local ports are Flask on `5000` and Expo Web on `8081`.

### Step 2 — Playable game

- Implement the title/setup, office map, mission, secret-room, and ending routes with Expo Router.
- Add the game reducer, player names, map hotspots, stats, fixed sample missions, and endings.
- Make a complete five-mission game playable before connecting generated content.

### Step 3 — Local AI missions

- Connect Flask to Ollama.
- Add the structured mission prompt, response validation, timeouts, and fallback missions.
- Replace sample mission selection with generated missions while preserving the fallback path.

### Step 4 — Map and visual identity

- Generate and approve the office-map artwork from the supplied references.
- Integrate the landscape map and align all responsive hotspots.
- Apply the Grand Task Office interface styling and lightweight sound effects.

### Step 5 — Items and special features

- Add inventory, object icons, item-powered choices, and acquisition animations.
- Add deterministic achievements.
- Add the keycard-and-document secret-room flow and special ending.

### Step 6 — Verification and demonstration

- Run the complete acceptance plan, including Ollama failure and fallback scenarios.
- Playtest the game with available colleagues and fix confusing or slow interactions.
- Prepare a short demonstration explaining Expo Router, React Native state, Flask validation, and local AI generation.

## 9. Test and acceptance plan

- All six normal hotspots align with the responsive map and support keyboard interaction.
- All five Expo routes work when opened directly in web mode and normal game navigation cannot lose reducer state.
- Every mission contains a title, situation, and exactly three choices.
- Money, reputation, and alert changes remain within allowed bounds.
- The five-round endings and immediate five-star ending work correctly.
- Awarded objects animate into inventory and remain available.
- Required objects are owned, consumed once, and never simultaneously rewarded by the same choice.
- The hidden room appears only when both required objects are collected.
- Player names appear safely in missions and reset between games.
- Achievement rules produce consistent results without relying on AI.
- Reduced-motion mode, restart, invalid JSON, timeout, stopped Ollama, and missing-model paths work correctly.
- A complete game remains playable through fallback missions without AI.
- No sensitive text or real branding from the reference images appears in the generated map.
- A group can complete the experience on one shared screen within 5–10 minutes.

## 10. Assumptions

- Ollama and `gemma3:4b` are installed and running on the host Mac.
- The supplied office images are authorized as design references for this internal project.
- The generated map will be a new visual interpretation, not a direct reproduction.
- The initial release is designed for one computer and a shared screen.
- The official demo target is Expo Web on the laptop; iOS, Android, and Expo Go support are learning extensions rather than presentation requirements.
- One developer owns and builds this project with extensive assistance from Codex, image generation, GitHub Copilot, and the local Ollama model.
- The 4–6 people mentioned in the game description are potential players, not the development team.
